newsitem.title: USA: Poll gives Clinton edge in North Carolina.
newsitem.headline: Poll gives Clinton edge in North Carolina.

text.p: President Clinton leads Republican challenger Bob Dole in North Carolina 49 percent to 40 percent, according to a poll released Monday by Raleigh's News and Observer newspaper and WTVD NewsChannel 11.

The poll said 5 percent of the voters favoured Reform Party candidate Ross Perot in the election Nov. 5. The statewide telephone poll of 607 likely voters was conducted Oct. 10-13 and had a margin of error of 4 percentage points, the newspaper said.
Voters were split over the Clinton administration's plans to regulate the tobacco industry, with 46 percent supporting the effort to classify nicotine as a drug and 49 percent opposing it.

North Carolina produces more tobacco than any other U.S. state, but only 2 percent of those polled said they planned to vote for Dole over Clinton because of the administration's stance. Three percent said they had switched from Dole to Clinton because of the issue, the newspaper said.

The News and Observer noted that another recent poll had Clinton trailing Dole in North Carolina. The Mason-Dixon Political/Media Research poll conducted last week showed Dole ahead with 48 percent to Clinton's 43 percent.
A recent CBS News poll of likely voters in North Carolina had Clinton ahead 49 percent to 43 percent.
